$comment: Findings `pnpm rls:check` is allowed to see on the acceptance database — the one
`tooling/scripts/verify-selfhost.mts` builds by running `rebase db push` over the reference
app's collections. Anything NOT listed here fails CI.
Every entry below is the same story: app/config/collections/index.ts declares
`{ operation: "select", access: "public" }` as the default rule, so the generator
correctly emits a SELECT policy with USING (true) for PUBLIC, and rls-check correctly
reports it. The finding is true; the access is intended. A public-read demo CMS is the
What this file still catches, which is why it is a per-table list and not a `--skip`:
a NEW collection arriving with public read that nobody thought about, the same check
firing on a table that is supposed to be private, and every other check on every table.
`target` is `schema.table` — never the policy name. Generated policy names carry a hash
of the rule's own semantics, so name-keyed entries would go stale on every unrelated
edit and the fix would be to paste in a new hash, which is how a baseline stops being
read. Matching ignores the policy name on purpose.
